status: Revised source numerical/actual-world checks passed; new native art and paired performance pending.
problem: The first wetland-complex native prototype passed runtime checks but still looked like ponds in short grass. Marked visually REJECTED rather than finished.
change: Add bounded shallow hollows to saturated margins of existing standing water and ordinary local ponds, retaining dry hummocks and the same accepted water head. Local ponds fade the cut to zero at their finite outer collar. Complexes already have their own hollows and do not receive a second cut.
hummock_revision: Complexes also allow bounded organic deposition, not just erosion, so low saturated ground can develop rooted/litter/peat mounds. Additional small-scale detail complements larger linked hollows. This is static morphology, not simulated peat growth.

hummock_research.application: Measured forested-wetland hummock height around 30cm above mean water level supports a decimetre-scale organic mound approximation.
Hummocks/tussocks can accumulate plant debris, roots and soil above surrounding saturated grade.

vegetation: Use existing local saturation in mid-plant suitability rather than only the broad habitat water table. Retain pH, salt, temperature, light and water-depth limits. Same candidate lattice and density ceiling. Reeds use green culms and fewer tube sides/segments; leaf/stem counts retained. Bare rock suppresses organic matter AFTER wet/peat floors, fixing an ordering error.
